flavors.text: You knew every bolt and gasket, but the books never added up. The lot went quiet one Tuesday, and it stayed that way.
You structured deals for Fortune 500s. In the end, your own ledger was the one that buried you.
Your father built this from nothing. You returned it to nothing.
They said you knew what was wrong before you sold it. The AG's office agreed.
Regulatory proceedings. The kind you used to advise clients to settle fast. You didn't.
The regulars who remembered your father remember something else now.
Twenty years in the shop, and it ends in a courtroom. The DA had the VINs memorized.
Wire fraud. The irony was not lost on anyone, least of all your former employer.
The family name made the headline. Your father would have understood — it was in the blood.
